# PointInstancer (rigid-body instancing)

Instances rigid-body prototypes. The runtime's rigid point-instancer loader reads the prototype targets and the per-instance arrays, parses each used prototype subtree once and stamps one body per active instance. It runs only when some [prim](glossary.md#prim) on the Stage applies PhysicsRigidBodyAPI or PhysicsCollisionAPI.

## What USD population writes

The producer gives a [PointInstancer](glossary.md#pointinstancer) a row when it reaches a physics prototype (see the [prim block](prim.md#columns)) and publishes its schema attributes at their resolved values. Population also preserves the authored prototype targets in order as prototypes:usd-targets, which the consumer prefers over the prototypes relationship.

## Columns

*Raw fallback* is the [USD](glossary.md#usd) schema value. *Producer writes* is what [ovstage](glossary.md#ovstage) population puts in the column for a USD stage. *Parser default* applies on the consumer when the column is absent, in stage units. **diverges** means writing the raw fallback literally parses differently from omitting the column (the parser default): USD population may well publish that very value for an unauthored attribute, so the marker is about the column being present, not about its value.

| Column | Type | Units | Raw fallback | Producer writes | Parser default | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prototypes` | uint64 array, RELATIONSHIP_PATH_ID |  |  | not written |  | No targets: every protoIndices entry is out of range and no instance is created. Consulted only when this prim has no prototypes:usd-targets row. |
| `prototypes:usd-targets` | uint64 array, RELATIONSHIP_PATH_ID |  |  | the authored prototypes targets in authored order |  | The prototypes relationship is read instead. A present but empty row is authoritative and does not fall back. |
| `protoIndices` | int32 array | none |  | not written |  | Warns that the indices array is not valid and creates no instance. |
| `positions` | float32[3] array, POINT | length |  | not written |  | Warns that the positions array is not valid; every instance is placed at the instancer origin. A length different from protoIndices warns the same way. |
| `orientations` | float16[4] array, QUATERNION | none |  | not written |  | Identity orientation per instance. A length different from protoIndices warns. |
| `velocities` | float32[3] array, VECTOR | length/s |  | not written |  | Zero initial linear velocity per instance. |
| `angularVelocities` | float32[3] array, VECTOR | deg/s |  | not written |  | Zero initial angular velocity per instance. |
| `scales` | float32[3] array | none |  | not written |  | Unit scale, and the instances share the prototype's shapes. With scales every instance gets its own scaled shapes. |
| `ids` | int64 array | none |  | not written |  | usd-metadata:inactiveIds names instances by position. |
| `usd-metadata:inactiveIds` | int64 array | none |  | the inactiveIds prim metadata |  | Every instance is active. |

## Interactions

- **[`PhysicsRigidBodyAPI`](PhysicsRigidBodyAPI.md):** Prototype subtrees are parsed as rigid bodies and colliders; a prototype that is not a body creates nothing per instance.
- **[`PhysxPhysicsJointInstancer`](PhysxPhysicsJointInstancer.md):** A joint instancer body target that is a PointInstancer resolves its body index through this prim's protoIndices and prototypes.

## Notes

- With PhysxParticleSetAPI applied, the particle-set parse reads positions and velocities as the particle positions and velocities (see PhysxParticleSetAPI); the descriptions here are the rigid-body path's.
